research_findings.headline: REQ-027 remine caught a real data-integrity bug -- an entire missed WIDE-bucket close (APU, span=17220s, -18.62%) had been silently absent from every prior tally, correcting count==3 WC span buckets from N=13 to N=14/15 and revealing WIDE performs worse than tracked (25%WR avg -3.88%, not 28.6%/-1.77%); REQ-030's full 12-mint CB repeat-mint audit found the pre-floor era shows NO trend-decline correlation with 2nd-entry outcome, so HBULL's post-floor loss remains N=1 and not gate-worthy; new hypothesis this run is post_bundle_priority_fee_dispersion, a cheap-to-build, zero-evidence-yet signal that reuses existing bundle-detection scaffolding.

new_hypothesis.name: post_bundle_priority_fee_dispersion
new_hypothesis.mechanism: In the 60-90s after a bundled pump.fun launch (multiple wallets buying in the same slot/bundle), if the priority fee / compute-unit price offered by DIFFERENT signers rises and disperses -- a real fee auction forming among independent buyers competing for block space -- that signals organic demand from unrelated wallets, not just the bundler's own sock-puppets recycling one flat fee. Rising/dispersed CU-price across distinct signers should predict further pump/graduation continuation; flat or clustered CU-price from what looks like the same wallet cluster signals it's still just the bundler inflating volume.
new_hypothesis.persistence: Fee-auction dynamics are a structural byproduct of Solana's leader-priority mechanism, not a pattern that gets arbitraged away by publishing it -- and no existing tool (Bubblemaps, GMGN, Trench Bot) surfaces it. This run's code check plus web research confirmed those tools all attack bundler detection via wallet-clustering/funding-graph analysis, a completely different axis from fee-competition intensity. It persists because extracting per-transaction CU-price and signer identity in a tight post-launch window is more instrumentation effort than the wallet-clustering tools bother with.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: Phase-1 LOG-ONLY. Reuse the existing _check_bundle_activity() hook (degen_bot.py:5687) that already flags bundle_detected+bundle_slot on buys -- no new detection logic needed, just extend it. When bundle_detected=true, poll the paid Alchemy RPC (getSignaturesForAddress / getTransaction on the pool address) for ~90s post-launch, extracting each subsequent buy tx's compute_unit_price and signer pubkey. Log signer_count, cu_price min/max/stddev, and same-signer-recurrence rate. No live filter change yet -- accumulate against forward 1h/24h token outcome to see if dispersion predicts continuation.
new_hypothesis.data_required: Alchemy Solana RPC (already paid/configured per project .env) via getTransaction with parsed instructions to read compute-unit price and signer. No new API keys or paid services needed.
new_hypothesis.evidence: Code check (this run): degen_bot.py already captures bundle_detected/bundle_slot per buy (_check_bundle_activity, line 5687) and two Jito aggregate-level pollers exist (tip_floor at line 5046, recent-bundles at line 5122, both research-148) but NONE captures per-signer CU-price dispersion -- zero grep hits for priority_fee/compute_unit_price/cu_price anywhere in degen_bot.py or sol_trade_log.json. Web research (this run): Jito docs confirm tips represent >60% of network priority-fee volume, validating the underlying economic mechanism is real, but zero papers/blogs/case studies found applying post-bundle CU-price dispersion specifically as a memecoin demand signal -- genuinely unexplored, not commoditized the way wallet-clustering already is.

request_responses.finding: Confirmed exactly 12 CB repeat-mint cases (matches the known candidate list exactly, including 2 distinct ROAR mints). Pre-floor era (N=11, April, ~0.010-0.019 SOL/trade): trend direction (mcap/h6/h24 declining vs improving between 1st and 2nd entry) shows NO correlation with 2nd-entry outcome -- 5 declining-trend cases split 4 good/1 bad, 6 improving-trend cases split 5 good/1 bad, both buckets net flat/positive regardless of direction (consistent with the old 'CB repeat-token 2nd+ outperforms 1st' finding, but that finding is driven by something other than fundamentals -- likely mean reversion / tiny stakes / short hold times, not trend-tracking). Post-floor era (N=1, HBULL only, ~0.10 SOL/trade, confirmed no other post-July-1 CB repeat-mint exists in the log): trend decline (mcap $4.10M->$2.77M, h6 +0.33%->-6.5%, h24 +94%->+8%, holder_top10 41.4%->47.49%) DID coincide with a bad 2nd-entry outcome (-11.98% after -15.43%), but remains a single data point. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT gate on trend-decline-since-last-entry -- the pre-floor sample actively argues against trend direction being reliable for this strategy, and post-floor has only HBULL. Need >=4 more comparable post-floor CB repeat-mint cases before revisiting; do not re-open until then.
